concerns.text: The plan records missing issue links as `null` and treats them as right‑censored, but later the latency analysis *excludes* any pair with a null latency (Wilcoxon test on latency). Excluding censored observations discards information and can bias the estimate of the latency difference.

Code churn is defined as the sum of lines added + deleted for a block, without normalizing for the block’s size (LOC). Larger blocks naturally have higher churn, which may confound the comparison between LLM‑generated and Human‑written code.

The a‑priori power analysis targets a medium effect size (rank‑biserial ≥ 0.3) for a paired Wilcoxon test, assuming complete, uncensored data. Because latency data will be censored and some churn observations may be missing, the calculated sample size (≥ 250 pairs) may be insufficient to achieve the claimed 80 % power.
